goal: Continuously improve the dotfiles repo toward a simple, reliable, fast implementation of its purpose (RUN.md): each cycle understand the real execution path, pick one evidence-backed improvement (correctness, then subtraction, then measured speed), implement it completely with a regression check, verify with the gate, report, repeat. Stop when no worthwhile evidence-backed improvement remains. The theme system (one palette script, thin callers, instant F6, F9 live preview, Enter applies, Esc restores) stays working throughout.

specs.instructions: Do `command_results` include, after the last edit to a theme file, running the picker's apply path with a scheme id and then printing tinty's current_scheme file showing that same id?

Do `command_results` include, after the last edit to a theme file, a preview of one scheme, then the picker's cancel/restore path, then a `tmux show` status-style output equal to the value printed before the preview?
Do `command_results` include, after the last edit to a theme file, two consecutive F6 toggles where the printed current_scheme after the second toggle equals the one printed before the first?
Do `command_results` include, after the last edit to a theme file, an F6 timing run that printed a line `painted_ms=N` where N is 300 or less?
Do `command_results` include, after the last edit to a theme file, a run of /tmp/ptytest.py against a freshly started tmux server whose output contains `fresh OSC4 seen: True`?

Do `command_results` include, after the last edit to a theme file, running the `tv theme` channel's preview command for one scheme id and then a `tmux show` output of status-style containing a hex colour different from the one shown before the preview?
In an isolated tmux + XDG tree: a new terminal gets the palette, F6 round-trips within 300 ms, preview retints, Esc restores exactly, Enter applies.
The `bounded` helper passes exit status through, returns 124 at its deadline, and leaves no process of the group alive either way.
Every tv channel the F8 overlay can open lists its rows within 2 s, with stdin closed, and leaves no process behind.
Scrolling the theme picker repaints nothing until the cursor stops, then paints the settled row.
Every theme, font and tv-go action exits and leaves no process behind (open, act, close, clean up).
Every background spawn (nohup), Keychain read, pass read and curl download under home/ and install.sh carries a deadline.
Two F3 searches (tv-go find, text channel) each closed with Esc: nothing the first started (tv, its rg source) still runs when the second starts, and nothing either started survives the run.
Nothing under home/ (code or manual) names a removed theme helper or the deleted preview script.
Exactly one file under home/ (outside the manual) reads the tinty scheme catalog — the one palette parser.
At most four theme files exist and they total at most 200 lines (baseline 5 files, 406 lines at HEAD).
Every tracked bash script runs on macOS /bin/bash 3.2: no mapfile/readarray, associative arrays, case-folding expansions or &>>.

F1 cockpit is laid out as which-key.nvim: multiple columns, `k ➜ icon label` with the key lit inside its label, actions before +groups, a » breadcrumb, the help line last, and group/Backspace keys move between menus.
F1 cockpit: tmux.conf parses and binds F1 to cockpit, every cockpit.tsv row is well-formed with an icon under a group, and every WezTerm action it sends is mapped in wezterm.lua.
In copy mode, Space selects and Enter opens the word on the row under the copy-mode cursor, also when the view is scrolled back or a wrapped line sits above the cursor.
fzf is invoked only from tv-go; everywhere else television or telescope is the picker.

The greppable hard-won constraints hold: nushell use_kitty_protocol false, no lualine auto theme, LSP log level capped, no literal chezmoi source path, tmux sync feature on and terminal-features never appended.
F1 leader (now the cockpit): tmux.conf parses, every cockpit.tsv row is well-formed under a group, and every WezTerm action it sends is mapped in wezterm.lua.
Every tracked Lua file (Neovim, WezTerm) compiles under luajit.
Regenerating the manual changes nothing: the committed manual matches its .nuon sources.
Every one-line code snippet in the nushell-modules and capsule internals pages still occurs in a tracked source file.
The memos gate (`just memos-check`) passes.
tinty owns the palette: no hex colour literal appears in home/ outside tinted-theming.

First check whether `actions_taken` edit or delete any file under `.orly/` (config.json, a check script, behaviour.py, or a spec). If NOT, answer yes. If one is edited, answer yes only when the diff shown adds or tightens a condition and removes or loosens none.
Every tracked nushell file parses without an error diagnostic (nu --ide-check).
A Ctrl-Q recent picked as a relative path (fd, rg) opens the file under the directory it was picked in, not under the shell's current directory.

First check whether `actions_taken` edit any file under `home/`, `scripts/`, `install.sh` or `justfile`. If NOT, answer yes. If one is edited, answer yes only when the final assistant message names what changed and which command output verified it.
Every tracked bash/sh script under home/ passes a syntax check.
Every tracked shell script under home/ and install.sh is shellcheck-clean at warning level.
Complexity ceiling: no tracked code file exceeds 500 lines and all tracked code under home/, install.sh, justfile and scripts/ stays at or under 4100 lines.

theme_size.command: bash -c 'n=0; for f in home/dot_config/tinted-theming/tinty/config.toml home/dot_config/tinted-theming/tinty/executable_theme.sh home/dot_config/television/cable/theme.toml home/dot_config/nushell/theme.nu home/dot_config/television/executable_theme-preview.sh home/dot_config/tinted-theming/tinty/executable_tmux-colors.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; l=$(cat home/dot_config/tinted-theming/tinty/config.toml home/dot_config/tinted-theming/tinty/executable_theme.sh home/dot_config/television/cable/theme.toml | wc -l); echo files=$n lines=$l; [ $n -le 4 ] && [ $l -le 200 ]'

manual_fresh.command: bash -c 'd=$(mktemp -d); cp -R home/dot_config/nushell/help/manual "$d"/m; just manual >/dev/null && diff -rq "$d"/m home/dot_config/nushell/help/manual'

scripts_parse.command: bash -c 'rc=0; for f in $(git ls-files home | grep -E "(\.sh$|/executable_)"); do head -1 "$f" | grep -q bash && { bash -n "$f" || { echo "$f"; rc=1; }; }; head -1 "$f" | grep -qE "^#!/bin/sh|env sh" && { sh -n "$f" || { echo "$f"; rc=1; }; }; done; exit $rc'

no_unbounded_wait.command: bash -c 'bad=$(rg -n "nohup|security find-generic-password|pass show" home install.sh --glob "!**/help/**" | grep -v bounded; rg -n "curl " install.sh home --glob "!**/help/**" --glob "!**/Dockerfile" | grep -v -- --max-time); echo "$bad"; [ -z "$bad" ]'

shellcheck.command: bash -c 'rc=0; for f in $(git ls-files home install.sh | grep -E "(\.sh$|/executable_|install\.sh$)"); do head -1 "$f" | grep -qE "bash|/sh" || continue; shellcheck -S warning -f gcc "$f" || rc=1; done; exit $rc'
